title: Aseptic technique and microbial culture; Cell theory, microscopes and magnification
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE01a#N.6, PR04b#N.4, CE01a#N.9, PR04b#N.11, CE01a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Stage micrometer
items.clue: A slide with a real scale, often 1 mm in 100 divisions

items.label: Scale bar
items.clue: A line on an image labelled with the actual length it represents

items.label: Magnification
items.clue: Image size divided by actual size; written with no unit, e.g. ×2000

items.label: Eyepiece graticule
items.clue: Scale seen down the microscope whose divisions have no fixed size until calibrated

questions.stem: In a photomicrograph taken at a magnification of ×2000, a red blood cell measures 15 mm across. What is the actual width of the cell?
questions.explanation: Actual size = 15 mm ÷ 2000 = 0.0075 mm, which is 7.5 µm (1 mm = 1000 µm): the typical diameter of a red blood cell.

questions.stem: A student spreads 0.2 cm³ of the 10⁻³ dilution of a culture onto agar. After incubation there are 86 colonies. What is the number of living cells per cm³ in the original culture?

With the ×40 objective lens in place, 40 divisions of an eyepiece graticule line up exactly with 100 µm on a stage micrometer. Using the same objective, a cell spans 44 graticule divisions. What is the actual length of the cell in millimetres?
questions.explanation: 100 µm ÷ 40 = 2.5 µm per division with this objective. 44 × 2.5 µm = 110 µm = 0.11 mm.

questions.stem: A student records the size of a duckweed population every two days and plots it on a logarithmic vertical axis against time on a non-logarithmic horizontal axis. Which observation would show that growth was exponential?

options.text: The points form a curve that becomes steeper with time, as exponential growth does on ordinary axes.
The points lie on a straight line, because a fixed number of plants was added in each two-day interval.
The points trace an S-shaped curve, because all populations grow according to the sigmoid model.
The points lie on a straight line, because the population multiplied by the same factor in each two-day interval.

questions.stem: A micrograph shows a pollen grain 60 mm across. A scale bar on the micrograph is 20 mm long and is labelled 10 µm. What is the actual diameter of the pollen grain?
questions.explanation: Magnification = 20 000 µm ÷ 10 µm = ×2000. Actual size = 60 000 µm ÷ 2000 = 30 µm.
